item.title: Hong Kong signals route to ride-hailing licences for private car owners
item.description: Hong Kong private car owners can apply for one of 10,000 ride-hailing vehicle permits under the quota system opening early next year, with higher chances given to those who have passed a combined driving test, already hold a ride-hailing driving permit, or have owned a private car for a designated period, according to transport authorities. item.title: Malaysian police close in on mastermind in air force drug-smuggling case
item.description: Malaysian police are closing in on the suspected ringleader of a drug-trafficking syndicate accused of using military assets to smuggle three tonnes of methamphetamine over more than two years, with a minister saying further arrests are expected “in the coming days”. Seven air force personnel were among 13 people arrested after police discovered nearly 97kg of methamphetamine on November 17 during a routine luggage check at the Subang Air Force Base, about 30km from the capital city of Kuala...

item.title: Hong Kong privacy watchdog urges businesses to ramp up investment in data security
item.description: Hong Kong’s privacy watchdog has urged businesses to invest more resources in strengthening their information technology systems in the wake of a recent string of cybersecurity breaches that have affected more than 1 million users. item.title: China and Netherlands send ‘positive signal’ over global controls on military AI
item.description: China and the Netherlands have agreed on the need for international regulations on the military use of AI, a move hailed as an encouraging step forward. The two countries agreed on the necessity of global cooperation on artificial intelligence and the opportunities and risks from the technology, according to a joint statement issued on Wednesday after Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met his Dutch counterpart, Tom Berendsen, in Beijing. item.title: China’s appetite for Russian farm goods grows despite thaw in US trade ties
item.description: From vegetable oil to seafood, Russia’s agricultural exports to China are hitting new milestones, even as US and Chinese officials move to stabilise a farm trade relationship increasingly overshadowed by geopolitics.
